title: SoftBank junk bond sale raises stakes for CEO Son's all-in AI bet
source_used: BigGo Finance's account of the Reuters report, with the opening paragraphs on The Japan Times (Reuters page returns HTTP 401; TradingView stub unreadable)
key_facts: SoftBank sold $10 billion of dollar notes and 1 billion euros of euro notes on 24 Sep 2026, the largest junk bond sale on record, with coupons reaching 9.75%, the highest SoftBank has ever promised.
Son has put a cumulative $64.6 billion into OpenAI; proceeds are earmarked for the final $10 billion of SoftBank's OpenAI commitment (BigGo).

Alex Clavel, chief executive of SoftBank Investment Advisers, told Reuters SoftBank borrowed because it does not want to sell assets it believes will keep rising; he called 9.75% 'still very reasonable' given OpenAI's appreciation.
David Gibson, an analyst at MST Financial: SoftBank was 'betting on a bunch of numbers at the roulette table'; now 'it's red or black'.
The bonds carry a BB+ rating, one notch below investment grade; Alphabet priced a 2033 bond at 5.2% in August (BigGo).
Arm accounts for about half of SoftBank's investment asset value, per S&P Global Ratings; SoftBank shares are down 38% from their June record (BigGo).
The Japan Times copy says the issuance added to a sharp surge in corporate borrowing this year, including major bond sales from Amazon, Alphabet and Tencent.
quote_evidence: SoftBank's promise to pay its highest-ever yields in a record $11 billion junk-bond offering highlights the pressure on CEO Masayoshi Son to secure returns on his all-in bet on artificial intelligence amid concerns about possible overheating in the market.
sold $10 billion of dollar notes and 1 billion euros of euro notes on September 24
"Given OpenAI's appreciation to date, 9.75 per cent is still very reasonable," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A record junk-bond sale at the highest yield SoftBank has paid shows how much rides on the OpenAI bet.
event_date: sale on 24 Sep 2026; Reuters analysis of 13 Oct 2026
notes: Reuters page returned HTTP 401; The Japan Times copy and TradingView stop after the opening paragraphs. BigGo Finance (finance.biggo.com) gives a long account of the Reuters report with direct quotes and is the source of the figures and quotes here; it is a summary by a third party, not the Reuters text, and the 24 Sep 2026 date is BigGo's. Reuters' 13 Oct analysis (C07-01) confirms the 9.75% coupon on a 7.5-year tranche and 'last month'. The 4 Oct 2026 edition mentioned the sale in passing in an Observer item.
